slides.say: A and B represent digits. Which of the following could be the value of A three, times B seven?
A product with letters, and we don't need the letters, just two facts. [short pause] We'll solve it with the units digit and the size.
[short pause] Fact one, only the units digits decide the units digit of a product. Three times seven is twenty-one, so the product ends in one. Eight fifty-seven ends in seven. Out.
Fact two, the size. The smallest is thirteen times seventeen, two twenty-one. So ninety-one is too small. Out.
The largest is ninety-three times ninety-seven, less than a hundred times a hundred, ten thousand. So ten thousand and one is too big. Out.

And eight fifty-one really happens. Twenty-three times thirty is six ninety, and twenty-three times seven is one sixty-one. Together, eight fifty-one. Choice number two is our answer. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
